mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates indicate tight monetary conditions, which increase borrowing costs and reduce corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is above 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP indicates strong economic demand, which boosts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but SPX 60-day returns are negative in >40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A falling unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, increasing consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE is below 4% but SPX 20-day returns are negative in >30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth indicates increased economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth exceeds 103 but SPX 60-day returns are negative in >40% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth combined with rising federal funds rates creates a restrictive economic environment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth slows AND FEDFUNDS rises
failure_condition: If GDPC1 slows and FEDFUNDS rises but SPX 60-day returns are positive in >50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates strong consumer demand in the housing market, which should positively impact related sectors and drive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST exceeds 1400 but SPX 20-day returns are negative in >30% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, which should increase consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth is positive but SPX 5-day returns are negative in >40% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPI) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE) creates a wage-price spiral, increasing costs for corporations and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises AND UNRATE stays below 4%
failure_condition: If CPI rises and UNRATE stays low but SPX 20-day returns are positive in >50% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.
